channel.title: Gaia's Secret Agents — Homeschool Nature Learning
channel.description: Outdoor learning, homeschool science and printable environmental activities for children.

item.title: Nature Walk Activity for Kids: A One-Minute Listening Mission
item.description: Try this simple outdoor listening activity together: stand still, listen for three different sounds and share what you noticed. An easy nature-study idea for a family walk or homeschool break. Save the prompt, then explore more screen-free nature activities and sound-map ideas from Gaia’s Secret Agents.

media:content.media:description: A kookaburra watches from a gum tree above a child and older adult, beside three steps for a family listening activity.

item.title: Backyard Nature Activity for Kids: A Tiny-World Safari
item.description: Go slow and spot more. Pause beside a plant, look for tiny movements and watch without disturbing wildlife. This simple backyard nature activity gives families and homeschoolers a reason to explore together. Save the three-step prompt, then visit Gaia’s Secret Agents for more mini nature missions.

media:content.media:description: A smiling parent and child observe a snail on a leaf, with three steps for a tiny-world safari.

item.title: Backyard Nature Study for Kids: A Free 5-Day Wildlife Tracker
item.description: How can children spot changes in a backyard habitat? Check the same little shelter each day and record the weather, visitors and clues. Watch wildlife without touching or feeding it. Get the free two-page tracker with a parent, guardian or teacher email.

media:content.media:description: Sunlight falls on a bark shelter resting on a mossy stone. The headline asks who visits one tiny patch of garden.

item.title: Five-Minute Nature Walk for Kids: Find Three Signs of Wildlife
item.description: How can you spot wildlife if the animal has already gone? Look for three signs such as a feather, a track or a nibbled leaf. Notice where each clue lies and leave it undisturbed. Try the free five-minute Nature Detective mission.

media:content.media:description: A pale feather lies beside seeds and a nibbled gum leaf in sunlit leaf litter. Text invites families to find three signs.

item.title: Homeschool Nature Journal: Spot a Spiderweb After Rain
item.description: What can a child record on a damp day? Note the weather, sketch a web you can see from the path and leave it in place. The free two-page Nature Tracker has room for five days of observations. Get the tracker with a parent, guardian or teacher email.

media:content.media:description: Water beads along a web between gum leaves. The headline invites children to observe after rain.
